answer: Anchor each agent to a physical location with latency triangulation. The network pings every identity from scattered beacons and measures round-trip times, so an agent perched on a shale ridge carries a different timing signature than one out past a dune. A thousand clones sharing one server all trace the same latency thread back to a single rack and collapse into one coordinate. To masquerade as N distinct network positions a sybil must rent N genuinely dispersed hosts, real machines in real places, a geographic cost no parallel fork can fabricate.
